questions.question_text: A function of the form $y=a\arccos(bx)$ has $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{1-16x^{2}}}$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive. What is $y$?

options.why: Ignored the minus sign in the given derivative, which points to $\arccos$ rather than $\arcsin$.
Read the inner coefficient off $16x^{2}$ as $16$ instead of taking its square root.
Ignored the minus sign and also read the inner coefficient as $16$ rather than $4$.

questions.solution_text:
The surd $\sqrt{1-16x^{2}}$ means $[f(x)]^{2}=16x^{2}$, so $f(x)=4x$.
$\dfrac{d}{dx}\arccos 4x=-\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{1-16x^{2}}}$
This matches the given derivative, so $a=1$ and $y=\arccos 4x$.
